This session found no evidence connecting that Cyxtera and Cologix history to the Centersquare, Csquare, or Evoque names researched for this batch, so the two threads are treated as distinct and unconfirmed to be related. This registry also carries a separate Csquare operator bucket, not part of this batch, whose name is now confirmed by the redirect evidence above to very likely be the same current brand as the Centersquare bucket this batch covers, though this session did not merge or rename either bucket, flagging this as an open duplicate operator naming question for a future dedicated pass rather than resolving it unilaterally. reading.body:
Centersquare Elk Grove Village ORD2 is a 147.6 MW campus in the Chicago suburbs, 3 miles from O'Hare. It qualifies to host SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, and NIST 800-53 workloads. The operator publishes no specific rack count or GPU allocation, so the intensity of use at this site is not disclosed; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 147.6 MW would support roughly 3,700 racks, but this campus may run at lower or higher intensity depending on tenant mix.

Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities and only 6 with published power figures totaling 236 MW; Centersquare Elk Grove Village ORD2 ranks seventh by published capacity in the state, meaning it sits just outside the state's ranked top tier. The campus is one of more than 80 facilities the operator manages across 15 North American markets and claims over 500 MW of total portfolio capacity, though this particular site is not among Illinois's largest disclosed campuses.

The published utility power of 147.6 MW reflects the campus constraint, not necessarily full build-out; the operator describes 111,906 square feet of raised floor at this location, which is below the 237,000 square feet listed in technical space on the spec page, suggesting headroom for expansion if power supply permits. Whether Centersquare can add capacity depends on Illinois grid availability and the binding regional power constraints, which are not published here.
